views.name: job_postings_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  j.job_id,
  j.company_id,
  c.name AS name,
  c.link AS link,
  c.link_google AS link_google,
  c.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
  j.job_title_short,
  j.job_title,
  j.job_location,
  j.job_via,
  j.job_schedule_type,
  j.job_work_from_home,
  j.search_location,
  j.job_posted_date,
  j.job_no_degree_mention,
  j.job_health_insurance,
  j.job_country,
  j.salary_rate,
  j.salary_year_avg,
  j.salary_hour_avg
FROM job_postings_fact AS j
LEFT JOIN job_company AS c
  ON j.company_id = c.company_id

params.description: A one-row-per-job enriched view combining job_postings_fact rows with their company attributes to answer questions about individual job postings and their company metadata.
params.when_to_use: List or detail of job postings with company info (e.g., show job title, location, company name, links, thumbnail, posted date, and salary fields). | Filterable job feed (e.g., jobs by country, location, schedule type, remote flag, posted date range). | Compose higher-level aggregations per job (e.g., count of distinct jobs, average salary across selected jobs) by aggregating this view. | Join to other one-row-per-entity dimensions (e.g., city, company profile, legislators_profile) to enrich job rows without duplicating job-level measures.
params.output_schema: job_id: unique identifier for the job posting — derived from job_postings_fact.job_id | company_id: foreign key referencing the hiring company — derived from job_postings_fact.company_id | name: company name for the job posting — derived from job_company.name | link: company website/link — derived from job_company.link | link_google: Google Maps or Google-specific link for the company — derived from job_company.link_google | thumbnail: company thumbnail image URL — derived from job_company.thumbnail | job_title_short: short/normalized job title string — derived from job_postings_fact.job_title_short | job_title: full job title text — derived from job_postings_fact.job_title | job_location: textual job location (city/region) as recorded in the posting — derived from job_postings_fact.job_location | job_via: source or channel showing where the job was posted (e.g., referral platform) — derived from job_postings_fact.job_via | job_schedule_type: schedule classification (e.g., full-time, part-time) — derived from job_postings_fact.job_schedule_type | job_work_from_home: flag/indicator for remote/WFH availability — derived from job_postings_fact.job_work_from_home | search_location: normalized/searchable location used when indexing the job — derived from job_postings_fact.search_location | job_posted_date: date when the job was posted — derived from job_postings_fact.job_posted_date | job_no_degree_mention: boolean/flag indicating posting does not mention a degree requirement — derived from job_postings_fact.job_no_degree_mention | job_health_insurance: boolean/flag indicating health insurance is mentioned/offered — derived from job_postings_fact.job_health_insurance | job_country: country code/name associated with the job posting — derived from job_postings_fact.job_country | salary_rate: salary rate unit or label (e.g., 'year', 'hour') — derived from job_postings_fact.salary_rate | salary_year_avg: average annual salary value (if present) — derived from job_postings_fact.salary_year_avg | salary_hour_avg: average hourly salary value (if present) — derived from job_postings_fact.salary_hour_avg
params.grounded_columns: job_postings_fact.job_id | job_postings_fact.company_id | job_company.company_id | job_company.name | job_company.link | job_company.link_google | job_company.thumbnail | job_postings_fact.job_title_short | job_postings_fact.job_title | job_postings_fact.job_location | job_postings_fact.job_via | job_postings_fact.job_schedule_type | job_postings_fact.job_work_from_home | job_postings_fact.search_location | job_postings_fact.job_posted_date | job_postings_fact.job_no_degree_mention | job_postings_fact.job_health_insurance | job_postings_fact.job_country | job_postings_fact.salary_rate | job_postings_fact.salary_year_avg | job_postings_fact.salary_hour_avg
params.metric: This view is at grain job_postings_fact.job_id (one row per job_id). No aggregate metrics are defined inside the view; salary_year_avg and salary_hour_avg are pass-through numeric columns from job_postings_fact and are not aggregated here. | If you need aggregated measures: e.g., jobs_count = COUNT(job_id) over a selection; avg_salary_year = AVG(salary_year_avg) computed by aggregating this view's rows.
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join this view to one-row-per-company/company-profile views on company_id (e.g., join to job_company or legislators_profile-like single-row company dimension) — safe because job_postings_enriched is one-row-per-job_id and joining to a single-row-per-company does not duplicate job rows. | Safe: join to cities_with_country or any city/dimension view keyed by job_location or search_location (if those dims are one-row-per-location) — safe because those dims are one-to-one with location keys and will not multiply job rows. | Safe: aggregate this view first before joining to one-to-many analytic tables. For example, to compute counts or averages per company, GROUP BY company_id on this view, producing one row per company, then join to other one-row-per-company resources. | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many child tables (e.g., skills_demand_by_job or other tables that list multiple skills per job) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply job-level rows and duplicate measures like salary_year_avg. Instead, either: |   - join aggregated child results keyed by job_id (e.g., skills_demand_by_job aggregated to one row per job_id) — safe because both sides will be one-row-per-job_id, or |   - aggregate this view up (e.g., GROUP BY job_id or company_id) and then join, depending on the target grain. | Examples of unsafe joins without re-aggregation: joining to skills_demand_by_job (AGG) at its many-rows-per-job form will multiply job rows; joining to cities_population_rank if that view contains multiple rows per location (check its grain) can also duplicate rows. | Planner tips: treat this view as a base fact at job_id grain. When composing higher-grain metrics, always aggregate job-level measures (counts, AVG(salary_year_avg), SUM(...)) before joining to any dimension that is many-to-one or many-to-many relative to job_id.

views.description: Denormalized job postings with company metadata and enriched salary measures. Useful as a starting relation for job-level analytics, filtering by company, location, date, or salary. | Use for: Average salary by country or company; Jobs by location or schedule type; Jobs with/without degree mentions; Company-level job counts and salary distributions

views.name: legislators_latest_term
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state,
  lt.district,
  lt.class,
  lt.party,
  lt.how,
  lt.url,
  lt.address,
  lt.phone,
  lt.fax,
  lt.contact_form,
  lt.office,
  lt.state_rank,
  lt.rss_url,
  lt.caucus,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_end DESC, lt.term_start DESC) AS term_rank
FROM legislators_terms AS lt

params.description: Provides the latest terms per legislator (ranked by term_end, term_start) and the full set of columns from legislators_terms for each legislator-term, with a term_rank (1 = most recent).
params.when_to_use: Find the most recent term(s) for a given legislator (e.g., current office or latest historical term). | Filter legislators to their latest term and then join to other tables (profiles, jobs, etc.) by legislator id or term id. | Compose time-aware analytics that need term-level attributes (party, state, district, office, contact information) for the latest term. | Build lists of current legislators (term_rank = 1) or compare current vs prior terms by joining back to this view on id_bioguide and term_rank.
params.output_schema: id_bioguide: Biographical identifier for the legislator; derived from legislators_terms.id_bioguide | term_number: Ordinal term number as stored in legislators_terms.term_number | term_id: Identifier for the specific term record; derived from legislators_terms.term_id | term_type: Type/category of the term (e.g., senate/house) from legislators_terms.term_type | term_start: Term start date/time from legislators_terms.term_start | term_end: Term end date/time from legislators_terms.term_end | state: State associated with the term from legislators_terms.state | district: District associated with the term from legislators_terms.district | class: Class (senate class or similar) from legislators_terms.class | party: Party affiliation during the term from legislators_terms.party | how: How the legislator attained the term (e.g., election, appointment) from legislators_terms.how | url: Public URL for the legislator/term from legislators_terms.url | address: Office mailing address for the term from legislators_terms.address | phone: Office phone number for the term from legislators_terms.phone | fax: Office fax number for the term from legislators_terms.fax | contact_form: Contact form URL for the term from legislators_terms.contact_form | office: Office name/location for the term from legislators_terms.office | state_rank: Rank within the state for the term (value from legislators_terms.state_rank) | rss_url: RSS feed URL for the legislator/term from legislators_terms.rss_url | caucus: Caucus membership or label for the term from legislators_terms.caucus | term_rank: Window function rank over (partition by id_bioguide order by term_end DESC, term_start DESC); 1 = most recent term for that legislator
params.grounded_columns: legislators_terms.id_bioguide | legislators_terms.term_number | legislators_terms.term_id | legislators_terms.term_type | legislators_terms.term_start | legislators_terms.term_end | legislators_terms.state | legislators_terms.district | legislators_terms.class | legislators_terms.party | legislators_terms.how | legislators_terms.url | legislators_terms.address | legislators_terms.phone | legislators_terms.fax | legislators_terms.contact_form | legislators_terms.office | legislators_terms.state_rank | legislators_terms.rss_url | legislators_terms.caucus
params.metric: term_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY legislators_terms.id_bioguide ORDER BY legislators_terms.term_end DESC, legislators_terms.term_start DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to legislators_profile on id_bioguide — safe because legislators_profile is expected to be one-row-per id_bioguide (1:1), so joining will not duplicate rows/measures from this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling view job_postings_enriched only when keyed by a single term_id (job_postings_enriched.term_id = legislators_latest_term.term_id) and job_postings_enriched is 1:1 per term_id; otherwise aggregate job_postings_enriched to term_id before joining to avoid duplicating legislator-term rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cities_with_country or cities_population_rank when mapping a single city value (e.g., office city) and you first normalize the office->city to a single city key; ensure the city dimension is one-row-per-city to keep joins safe. | unsafe-to-join-without-aggregation: do NOT directly join to inherently one-to-many tables (for example: job_postings_enriched, skills_demand_by_job, job_postings_salary_agg_by_country if they are at a finer grain) without first aggregating those tables to the legislators_latest_term grain (id_bioguide or term_id). Direct joins to many-side tables will multiply legislator-term rows and incorrectly duplicate any measures derived from this view. | unsafe-to-join-without-aggregation: do NOT join to tables keyed only on id_bioguide if those tables contain multiple rows per id_bioguide (for example, a history table of contacts) unless you aggregate that table to one row per id_bioguide prior to joining. | practical composition pattern: to combine counts/metrics from a many-side table, first produce an aggregate keyed by the same grain as this view (id_bioguide or term_id). Example: derive job_counts_by_term AS (SELECT term_id, COUNT(*) AS job_count FROM job_postings_enriched GROUP BY term_id) then LEFT JOIN job_counts_by_term ON legislators_latest_term.term_id = job_counts_by_term.term_id — safe because aggregation prevents row multiplication. | filtering note: to obtain current legislators, filter WHERE term_rank = 1. After filtering to term_rank = 1, joins to other 1:1 dimensions (by id_bioguide or term_id) remain safe; joins to many-side detail tables still require aggregation.

views.description: Latest term per legislator (by term_end). One row per id_bioguide with the most recent term record. Useful to get current/stateful legislator attributes derived from terms (e.g., current office, state, party). | Use for: Current office/party/state for a legislator; Filtering to latest term (WHERE term_rank = 1) to join to legislator person table; Counts of incumbents by party or state

views.name: legislators_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.id_bioguide,
  l.full_name,
  l.first_name,
  l.last_name,
  l.middle_name,
  l.nickname,
  l.suffix,
  l.other_names_end,
  l.other_names_middle,
  l.other_names_last,
  l.birthday,
  l.gender,
  l.id_bioguide_previous_0,
  l.id_govtrack,
  l.id_icpsr,
  l.id_wikipedia,
  l.id_wikidata,
  l.id_google_entity_id,
  l.id_house_history,
  l.id_house_history_alternate,
  l.id_thomas,
  l.id_cspan,
  l.id_votesmart,
  l.id_lis,
  l.id_ballotpedia,
  l.id_opensecrets,
  l.id_fec_0,
  l.id_fec_1,
  l.id_fec_2,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state AS state,
  lt.district AS district,
  lt.party AS party,
  lt.office AS office
FROM legislators AS l
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT
      lt.*,
      RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_end DESC, lt.term_start DESC) AS term_rank
    FROM legislators_terms AS lt
  ) WHERE term_rank = 1
) AS lt
  ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide

params.description: Provides one-row-per-legislator demographic & identifier profile enriched with that legislator's most-recent term (state/district/party/office) — answers who a legislator is and their current/latest seat.
params.when_to_use: Look up a legislator's biographical details and canonical identifiers (bioguide, govtrack, wikidata, etc.). | Find the latest/most-recent term (state, district, party, office, term start/end) for each legislator. | Join legislator-level facts to other datasets keyed by id_bioguide (e.g., vote records, sponsorships) when you need one row per legislator. | Compose additional aggregations at the legislator grain (e.g., count of bills sponsored per legislator) by joining on id_bioguide safely.
params.output_schema: id_bioguide: Unique legislator identifier from legislators.id_bioguide (primary key/grain). | full_name: Full display name from legislators.full_name. | first_name: Given name from legislators.first_name. | last_name: Family name from legislators.last_name. | middle_name: Middle name from legislators.middle_name. | nickname: Nickname from legislators.nickname. | suffix: Name suffix from legislators.suffix. | other_names_end: Other_names_end from legislators.other_names_end (alternate name fields as stored). | other_names_middle: Other_names_middle from legislators.other_names_middle. | other_names_last: Other_names_last from legislators.other_names_last. | birthday: Date of birth from legislators.birthday. | gender: Gender as recorded in legislators.gender. | id_bioguide_previous_0: Prior bioguide id from legislators.id_bioguide_previous_0. | id_govtrack: GovTrack identifier from legislators.id_govtrack. | id_icpsr: ICPSR identifier from legislators.id_icpsr. | id_wikipedia: Wikipedia page identifier from legislators.id_wikipedia. | id_wikidata: Wikidata Q-id from legislators.id_wikidata. | id_google_entity_id: Google knowledge graph id from legislators.id_google_entity_id. | id_house_history: HouseHistory id from legislators.id_house_history. | id_house_history_alternate: Alternate house history id from legislators.id_house_history_alternate. | id_thomas: Thomas id from legislators.id_thomas. | id_cspan: C-SPAN id from legislators.id_cspan. | id_votesmart: VoteSmart id from legislators.id_votesmart. | id_lis: LIS id from legislators.id_lis. | id_ballotpedia: Ballotpedia id from legislators.id_ballotpedia. | id_opensecrets: OpenSecrets id from legislators.id_opensecrets. | id_fec_0: FEC id (fec_0) from legislators.id_fec_0. | id_fec_1: FEC id (fec_1) from legislators.id_fec_1. | id_fec_2: FEC id (fec_2) from legislators.id_fec_2. | term_id: Identifier for the selected latest term from legislators_terms.term_id (via lt.term_id). | term_type: Term type (e.g., 'sen', 'rep') from legislators_terms.term_type (lt.term_type). | term_start: Term start date from legislators_terms.term_start (lt.term_start). | term_end: Term end date from legislators_terms.term_end (lt.term_end). | state: State for the latest term from legislators_terms.state (lt.state). | district: District for the latest term from legislators_terms.district (lt.district). | party: Party for the latest term from legislators_terms.party (lt.party). | office: Office for the latest term from legislators_terms.office (lt.office).
params.grounded_columns: legislators.id_bioguide | legislators.full_name | legislators.first_name | legislators.last_name | legislators.middle_name | legislators.nickname | legislators.suffix | legislators.other_names_end | legislators.other_names_middle | legislators.other_names_last | legislators.birthday | legislators.gender | legislators.id_bioguide_previous_0 | legislators.id_govtrack | legislators.id_icpsr | legislators.id_wikipedia | legislators.id_wikidata | legislators.id_google_entity_id | legislators.id_house_history | legislators.id_house_history_alternate | legislators.id_thomas | legislators.id_cspan | legislators.id_votesmart | legislators.id_lis | legislators.id_ballotpedia | legislators.id_opensecrets | legislators.id_fec_0 | legislators.id_fec_1 | legislators.id_fec_2 | legislators_terms.term_id | legislators_terms.term_type | legislators_terms.term_start | legislators_terms.term_end | legislators_terms.state | legislators_terms.district | legislators_terms.party | legislators_terms.office
params.metric: no row-level aggregates are produced by this view; all output columns are direct projections from base tables or the picked latest-term row. (i.e., no derived aggregate metrics like SUM/COUNT are defined here).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables or one-row-per-legislator views on id_bioguide without re-aggregation — safe because this view has one row per legislators.id_bioguide (the LEFT JOIN to the latest-term subquery picks at most one term row per id_bioguide). Example: join legislators_profile lp ON lp.id_bioguide = other_table.id_bioguide. | You can safely join to siblings that are also one-row-per-legislator (e.g., a hypothetical legislators_stats view aggregated to id_bioguide) on id_bioguide; measures from those views will not be multiplied. | Do NOT freely join this view to any one-to-many table or view (e.g., legislators_terms without limiting/aggregating, vote records, sponsorships, job_postings_enriched if it is one-to-many per legislator) on id_bioguide without first aggregating the many-side. Such joins will multiply rows and duplicate any aggregated measures. Instead: aggregate the many-side to id_bioguide (SUM/COUNT/etc.) or join via a subquery that returns one row per id_bioguide (for example, count of bills per legislator derived from bills grouped by sponsor_id_bioguide). | Specific safe join keys & rationale: | - Safe: join to any table/view keyed one-to-one with legislators.id_bioguide (e.g., a maintained legislator_metadata view) on id_bioguide — remains one row per legislator. | - Unsafe without aggregation: join to legislators_terms (raw) on id_bioguide — because legislators_terms contains multiple term rows per legislator and would create multiple output rows per id_bioguide. If you need term-level detail, join to legislators_terms and then either restrict (e.g., WHERE term_id = lp.term_id) or aggregate. | - Unsafe without aggregation: join to transactional or event tables (votes, speeches, job_postings_enriched when many postings per legislator) — aggregate those to id_bioguide first (e.g., COUNT(*) AS postings_count GROUP BY id_bioguide) before joining. | Planner guidance for composition: treat this view as a dimension with unique key id_bioguide. When building larger queries, push any many-side grouping/aggregation before joining to this view to avoid accidental row multiplication.

views.description: Legislator personal profile joined with their latest term to expose person + current-term attributes. One row per legislator (when filtered to latest term). Useful for personnel lists, contact info, and joining to term-based measures. | Use for: List current legislators with contact/party/state information; Join legislators to term-based vote or bill data (if available); Counts by party/state for current incumbents

views.name: cities_with_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id,
  c.city_name,
  c.latitude,
  c.longitude,
  c.country_code_2,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
  cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
  curr.currency_name AS currency_name,
  curr.currency_code AS currency_code,
  c.capital,
  c.population,
  c.insert_date
FROM cities AS c
LEFT JOIN cities_countries AS cc
  ON lower(c.country_code_2) = lower(cc.country_code_2)
LEFT JOIN cities_currencies AS curr
  ON lower(c.country_code_2) = lower(curr.country_code_2)

params.description: Provides one-row-per-city details enriched with country and currency attributes (location, administrative regions, currency, population and metadata).
params.when_to_use: Look up attributes for a specific city by city_id or city_name | Build country-level rollups after aggregating or re-aggregating city-level measures (for example, sum of population by country) | Map or visualize cities with their coordinates and associated country/currency attributes | Filter or join other datasets to cities while preserving one-row-per-city grain
params.output_schema: city_id: unique identifier for the city — derived from cities.city_id | city_name: human-readable name for the city — derived from cities.city_name | latitude: city's latitude coordinate — derived from cities.latitude | longitude: city's longitude coordinate — derived from cities.longitude | country_code_2: two-letter country code associated with the city — derived from cities.country_code_2 | country_name: full country name matched from cities_countries.country_name (via lower(country_code_2) join) | country_code_3: three-letter country code matched from cities_countries.country_code_3 (via lower(country_code_2) join) | region: top-level region matched from cities_countries.region (via lower(country_code_2) join) | sub_region: sub-region matched from cities_countries.sub_region (via lower(country_code_2) join) | intermediate_region: intermediate region matched from cities_countries.intermediate_region (via lower(country_code_2) join) | currency_name: currency name matched from cities_currencies.currency_name (via lower(country_code_2) join) | currency_code: currency code matched from cities_currencies.currency_code (via lower(country_code_2) join) | capital: boolean/flag (or text) from cities.capital indicating if the city is a capital — derived from cities.capital | population: population count for the city — derived from cities.population | insert_date: ingestion or insert timestamp for the city row — derived from cities.insert_date
params.grounded_columns: cities.city_id | cities.city_name | cities.latitude | cities.longitude | cities.country_code_2 | cities.capital | cities.population | cities.insert_date | cities_countries.country_name | cities_countries.country_code_3 | cities_countries.region | cities_countries.sub_region | cities_countries.intermediate_region | cities_currencies.currency_name | cities_currencies.currency_code
params.metric: population = cities.population  -- atomic, stored per city (no aggregation in view) | There are no aggregate metrics defined in this view. All columns are passed-through attributes from base tables or lookups (no SUM/COUNT/AVG/etc).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables keyed by city_id (or other one-to-one keys) without re-aggregation — e.g., join to a city-level enrichment view on cities_with_country.city_id = other.city_id is safe because cities_with_country has one row per city_id. | Safe to join to 'legislators_profile' or other one-row-per-city or one-row-per-person views when those views are keyed 1:1 to city_id or when you are joining on person_id/legislator_id that uniquely identifies rows — this will not duplicate city-level measures because this view's grain is city_id. | DO NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables or views (for example, job_postings_enriched, skills_demand_by_job, job_postings_salary_agg_by_country, or any raw job_postings table) without aggregating the many-side first. Reason: those are one-to-many relative to this view's city_id (a city can have many job postings). Directly joining would multiply city-level rows and duplicate city attributes and the population measure. Instead, aggregate the many-side (e.g., COUNT(job_id) or SUM(salary) grouped by city_id or country_code_2) and then join the aggregated result to cities_with_country on city_id or country_code_2. | When joining on country_code_2: this view uses cities.country_code_2 as its country key. Joining cities_with_country to country-level aggregates (for example job_postings_salary_agg_by_country) on lower(city.country_code_2) = lower(agg.country_code_2) is safe only if the country-level dataset is truly one-row-per-country. If the country-side is one-to-many, aggregate it before joining to avoid duplicating city rows. | When combining into higher-level rollups (e.g., population by country), compute aggregates from this view by grouping on country_code_2 (or country_name) — e.g., SUM(population) GROUP BY country_code_2 — rather than joining this view to city-many datasets and then aggregating, to maintain correct counts. | Null/missing country or currency lookups: the view uses LEFT JOINs to bring in country and currency attributes. Some cities may have NULLs for country_name/currency_code; treat those as unmatched lookup rows rather than additional rows — joins will not duplicate rows because joins are LEFT and keyed on equality of lower(country_code_2).

views.description: City dimension enriched with country attributes (country name, region, sub_region) and currency code where available. One row per city preserving city-level identifiers and country codes. | Use for: City population by country or region; Map city coordinates with region/currency metadata; Identify capital cities and their country attributes

views.name: alien_profiles
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.first_name AS first_name,
  a.last_name AS last_name,
  a.email AS email,
  a.gender AS gender,
  a.type AS type,
  a.birth_year AS birth_year,
  ad.age AS age,
  ad.favorite_food AS favorite_food,
  ad.feeding_frequency AS feeding_frequency,
  ad.aggressive AS aggressive,
  al.current_location AS current_location,
  al.state AS state,
  al.country AS country,
  al.occupation AS occupation
FROM aliens AS a
LEFT JOIN alien_data AS ad
  ON a.id = ad.id
LEFT JOIN aliens_location AS al
  ON a.id = al.loc_id
LEFT JOIN aliens_details AS d
  ON a.id = d.detail_id

params.description: A denormalized, one-row-per-alien profile combining core alien attributes, supplemental data, and location/occupation details to support profiling, filtering, and further aggregation by alien id.
params.when_to_use: Get the full profile for a specific alien id or a set of alien ids (SELECT by id or WHERE id IN (...)). | Filter or group aliens by demographic attributes (gender, type, birth_year, age, country, state, occupation). | Compose higher-level aggregations keyed by alien id (e.g., count of profiles, joins to events keyed by alien id) while preserving one-row-per-alien semantics. | Enrich other alien-centric datasets (events, transactions, sightings) by joining on alien id. | Build downstream aggregated metrics (e.g., counts by country or occupation) by aggregating this view, not by joining a one-to-many child directly.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the alien profile — derived from aliens.id | first_name: alien's first name — derived from aliens.first_name | last_name: alien's last name — derived from aliens.last_name | email: alien's email address — derived from aliens.email | gender: alien's gender attribute — derived from aliens.gender | type: alien classification/type — derived from aliens.type | birth_year: year of birth for the alien — derived from aliens.birth_year | age: age value taken from supplemental data — derived from alien_data.age (left-joined) | favorite_food: favorite food from supplemental data — derived from alien_data.favorite_food (left-joined) | feeding_frequency: how often the alien feeds — derived from alien_data.feeding_frequency (left-joined) | aggressive: aggressive flag/indicator — derived from alien_data.aggressive (left-joined) | current_location: textual/current location — derived from aliens_location.current_location (left-joined) | state: state of the current location — derived from aliens_location.state (left-joined) | country: country of the current location — derived from aliens_location.country (left-joined) | occupation: occupation taken from location/details table — derived from aliens_location.occupation (left-joined)
params.grounded_columns: aliens.id | aliens.first_name | aliens.last_name | aliens.email | aliens.gender | aliens.type | aliens.birth_year | alien_data.id | alien_data.age | alien_data.favorite_food | alien_data.feeding_frequency | alien_data.aggressive | aliens_location.loc_id | aliens_location.current_location | aliens_location.state | aliens_location.country | aliens_location.occupation | aliens_details.detail_id
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All output columns are base columns or direct projections from joined tables. (No derived aggregates like SUM/COUNT are present.)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to fact/event tables or other one-row-per-alien views on aliens.id (this view's id) — e.g., join events ON events.alien_id = alien_profiles.id — safe because alien_profiles is one-row-per-alien (aliens.id is the grain) so measures sourced from this view will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to sibling one-row-per-entity views keyed by country or state AFTER aggregating this view by country/state — safe pattern: SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM alien_profiles GROUP BY country; then join aggregated result to country-level dimension views. | DO NOT directly join this view to one-to-many child tables or views (for example: an aliens_telemetry table with multiple rows per alien, or any detailed sightings table) without re-aggregation — such joins would multiply rows for an alien and implicitly duplicate any counts or sums derived from this view. Instead, either: |   - aggregate the child to one row per alien first (e.g., SELECT alien_id, SUM(metric) AS metric_sum FROM child GROUP BY alien_id) then join to alien_profiles ON id = alien_id; or |   - aggregate alien_profiles to the desired grain (e.g., by country or occupation) and then join the child aggregated at the same grain. | AVOID joining to aliens_details (aliens_details.detail_id) if aliens_details is one-to-many per alien unless you intend to expand the profile into multiple rows per alien — the view's SQL LEFT JOIN to aliens_details is currently present but selects no columns from it, so composition guidance: confirm cardinality of aliens_details before joining other views that rely on those detail rows. | If composing additional measures based on this view, treat every column as a base attribute (no hidden aggregates). When producing aggregated metrics at a coarser grain, compute aggregates from this view (e.g., COUNT(id), AVG(age), COUNT(DISTINCT email) where appropriate) rather than joining-first to avoid accidental row multiplication.

views.description: Combined alien/person profile by joining core aliens with enriched data and location/details where keys align. Preserves identity columns and exposes favorite_food, feeding_frequency, aggressive, occupation, and location attributes. Useful for demographic and behavior analysis of aliens. | Use for: Demographic breakdowns of aliens (age, gender, type); Behavior/feeding patterns by region or occupation; Counts of aggressive aliens or favorite food distributions

views.name: cities_population_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  city_name,
  country_code_2,
  population,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code_2 ORDER BY population DESC) AS population_rank
FROM cities

params.description: Ranks cities by population within each 2-letter country, returning one row per city with its within-country population rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the most/least populous cities per country (e.g., top-N cities in each country). | Filter or aggregate only cities by their within-country population rank (e.g., select capitals or top-ranked cities). | Compose with other city-level or country-level data while preserving a single row per city.
params.output_schema: city_id: unique identifier for the city — sourced from cities.city_id | city_name: human-readable city name — sourced from cities.city_name | country_code_2: ISO 2-character country code for the city — sourced from cities.country_code_2 | population: population count for the city — sourced from cities.population | population_rank: rank of the city within its country by population (1 = largest) — derived using RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code_2 ORDER BY population DESC) applied to cities.population partitioned by cities.country_code_2
params.metric: population_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cities.country_code_2 ORDER BY cities.population DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to city dimension or 1:1 enrichment views on city_id — e.g., join to cities_with_country on city_id — safe because cities_population_rank has exactly one row per city_id, so measures (population, population_rank) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to legislators_profile or legislators_latest_term only if joining on city_id where those views are known to have at most one row per city_id (verify their grain) — safe when the other side is one-row-per-city. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as job_postings_enriched, job_postings_salary_agg_by_country (if that view is aggregated at country but job_postings_enriched is per-posting) or skills_demand_by_job without re-aggregating, because joining this city-level view to a many-row-per-city source will multiply city rows and thus duplicate population and population_rank measures. Instead, either: | - aggregate the many-side to city_id first (e.g., SUM(posting_count) GROUP BY city_id) and then join on city_id, or | - join only to country-level aggregates on country_code_2 (e.g., job_postings_salary_agg_by_country) when you intend to analyze at country granularity — joining on country_code_2 is safe because population_rank is a city-level measure and the join will produce multiple city rows per country by design; if you want to preserve non-duplicated country metrics, aggregate after the join appropriately. | When composing further ranked/ordered measures, be aware this view's population_rank uses RANK() which may produce ties — if you need dense ranks or tie-breaking, compute a new rank in the composed query using this view's population and country_code_2 as inputs.

views.description: Cities ranked by population within each country_code_2. One row per city with a population_rank to enable top-k per country filtering downstream. | Use for: Top N largest cities by country; Rank-based city selections for mapping or reporting; Comparing city populations within a country

views.name: job_postings_salary_agg_by_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_country,
  COUNT(job_id) AS job_posting_count,
  AVG(salary_year_avg) AS avg_salary_year,
  AVG(salary_hour_avg) AS avg_salary_hour
FROM job_postings_fact
GROUP BY job_country

params.description: Aggregated counts and average salary metrics for job postings at the country level.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of job postings and average salaries per country (yearly and hourly). | Compare job posting volume and average pay between countries. | Use as a country-level salary/volume base when composing larger analyses (e.g., join to country-level demographics) provided joins are cardinality-safe. | As a pre-aggregated source for dashboards or reports that require one row per job_country.
params.output_schema: job_country: ISO/normalized country identifier or country name used in job_postings_fact.job_country — the grouping key for this view. | job_posting_count: COUNT(job_id) from job_postings_fact — total number of job_postings aggregated for this job_country. | avg_salary_year: AVG(salary_year_avg) from job_postings_fact — average of the per-posting yearly salary estimate across postings in the country. | avg_salary_hour: AVG(salary_hour_avg) from job_postings_fact — average of the per-posting hourly salary estimate across postings in the country.
params.metric: job_posting_count = COUNT(job_postings_fact.job_id)  -- cardinality: counts rows (postings) per job_country | avg_salary_year = AVG(job_postings_fact.salary_year_avg)  -- arithmetic mean of salary_year_avg values per job_country | avg_salary_hour = AVG(job_postings_fact.salary_hour_avg)  -- arithmetic mean of salary_hour_avg values per job_country
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-country dimension/views on job_country — safe because this view is one-row-per-job_country, so measures will not be duplicated. Examples: join to cities_with_country (if that view provides a single row per country) OR to a country-level demographic view (if that view is one row per country). | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed by job_country without re-aggregation, because that would multiply job_posting_count and distort avg_salary_* unless you re-aggregate after the join. Examples of unsafe joins: joining to cities_with_country if that view is one row per city (many cities per country), joining to legislators_latest_term or legislators_profile (multiple legislators per country), or joining to cities_population_rank (if multiple rows per country). | If you must combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., city-level or legislator-level rows), either: |   - aggregate the child to country first (e.g., SUM/AVG per job_country) and then join country-to-country, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the result grouping by job_country to recompute job_posting_count and weighted/unweighted salary metrics correctly. | Notes on avg metrics when composing: avg_salary_year and avg_salary_hour are simple averages of posting-level salary_* values. If you join additional rows per job_country and want to preserve correct posting-weighted averages, compute AVG over the original posting-level values (or use SUM(salary_* * posting_weight)/SUM(posting_weight) where posting_weight = 1 per posting). Because this view stores only the aggregated mean and count, recomputing a correct global mean after joining other sources typically requires the underlying sums or counts; if composition requires exact weighted recomputation, re-aggregate from job_postings_fact or carry both count and sum (sum = avg * count) before joining. | Example safe join clause format: ON job_postings_salary_agg_by_country.job_country = <country_dim>.country_key (safe only if <country_dim> is 1:1 with country). | Example unsafe join clause (do NOT do without re-aggregation): ON job_postings_salary_agg_by_country.job_country = cities_with_country.job_country if cities_with_country contains multiple cities per country — this will multiply job_posting_count and distort avg_salary_*.

views.description: Aggregated salary measures per job_country: count of postings and average salary (year/hour). Useful for country-level salary comparisons and trend baselines. | Use for: Average salary by country; Number of job postings per country; Compare hourly vs yearly salary averages across countries

views.name: skills_demand_by_job
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.skill_id,
  s.skills,
  s.type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT j.job_id) AS jobs_with_skill,
  COUNT(j.job_id) AS skill_job_mappings
FROM skills_dim AS s
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim AS j
  ON s.skill_id = j.skill_id
GROUP BY s.skill_id, s.skills, s.type

params.description: Counts of distinct jobs and total skill-job mappings per skill — useful for understanding demand (how many job postings reference each skill) and how many mappings exist between skills and jobs.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of job postings that reference each skill (skill-level demand). | Rank or filter skills by how many jobs require them (e.g., top N most-demanded skills). | Join to skill metadata (skills text or type) while preserving one row per skill. | Compose with other aggregated datasets (e.g., country- or time-buckets of job counts) when combining on skill_id after re-aggregation if necessary.
params.output_schema: skill_id: unique identifier for the skill — derived from skills_dim.skill_id | skills: textual name/label of the skill — derived from skills_dim.skills | type: categorical type/classification of the skill — derived from skills_dim.type | jobs_with_skill: count of distinct job postings that reference this skill — derived as COUNT(DISTINCT skills_job_dim.job_id) | skill_job_mappings: total number of skill-to-job mappings (each row in skills_job_dim for this skill) — derived as COUNT(skills_job_dim.job_id)
params.metric: jobs_with_skill = COUNT(DISTINCT skills_job_dim.job_id)  -- counts unique job_id values joined to a skill_id | skill_job_mappings = COUNT(skills_job_dim.job_id)  -- counts all rows in skills_job_dim for the skill (includes duplicates if same job-skill appears multiple times)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to skill-level dimension or one-row-per-skill views on skill_id (e.g., skills_dim) — safe because skills_demand_by_job is one-row-per-skill, so joining another one-row-per-skill source will not duplicate its measures. | Safe to join on skill_id to sibling aggregated/rolled-up views that are also one-row-per-skill (if such exist) — the measures remain aligned and not multiplied. | Do NOT join directly to skills_job_dim (or any raw skills-to-job mapping table) without re-aggregating the joined data first — skills_job_dim is many-to-one into skill_id and would duplicate jobs_with_skill and skill_job_mappings counts if you join at the raw mapping level. | Do NOT join to job_postings_enriched (a JOIN producing many rows per job) or other job-level tables without first aggregating those tables to one row per job (or per skill-job as appropriate) — joining them directly would multiply counts because skills_demand_by_job already contains aggregated counts over skills_job_dim. | If you need breakdowns by another dimension (e.g., country or date), aggregate that other dimension at the job level (one row per job or per job-country-date bucket) and then join or re-aggregate by skill_id to avoid duplicating counts. For example: (1) compute job-level counts by country/date, (2) join job -> skills_job_dim and then re-aggregate per skill and country/date to produce correct per-skill per-country counts. | When composing further measures that sum or average jobs_with_skill or skill_job_mappings across joined dimensions, ensure you aggregate after joining (e.g., SUM(jobs_with_skill) is only valid if the join does not introduce multiplicative duplicates or if you first collapse the other side to one row per skill).

views.description: Counts of distinct jobs and occurrences per skill. One row per skill (skill_id) with measures for number of jobs that reference the skill and total mappings. | Use for: Most in-demand skills by job count; Skill popularity and density across job postings; Skill type rollups
